findings.assumptions: The openness claim rests on (i) the nine literature searches captured on 2026-10-21 (arXiv API and OpenAlex) for the exact statement and the eight declared neighbours, (ii) complete full-text readings of the seventeen works marked relevant, and (iii) the record's description of the reported September 2026 counterexample H0 (35 vertices, 66 edges; by the neighbour statement its 1-subdivision has 101 vertices, 132 edges and girth 8, and by the Conlon-Lee reading note it is the vertex-face incidence graph of a 13-vertex triangulated sphere, 22 faces). That description is internally consistent (Euler: 2V-4 = 22 faces; 13+22 = 35; 3*22 = 66; girth(S(H0)) = 8 implies girth(H0) = 4) and a vertex-face incidence graph of a triangulation contains 4-cycles, so H0 lies outside the class; the counterexample manuscript itself is not in evidence, but the openness verdict does not depend on it: if it does not exist the statement is a subcase of the previously open Sidorenko conjecture, and if it exists as described it has 4-cycles. The equivalence between the graphon form and the finite-host form is the standard graph-limit fact and is asserted in the resolution criteria, not proved in evidence; it is not needed for openness.

openness.reason: No captured work states or settles the statement. The positive results among the fully read works cover only strict subclasses of the girth-six bipartite graphs: trees, even cycles and the C6-based patterns; 1-subdivisions of KNRS graphs and of Sidorenko graphs (CKLL 2018, Theorem 1.3 and 3.1), odd subdivisions of KNRS graphs (Chen-Lin-Ma 2024), 1-subdivisions of regular-KNRS and Sidorenko-good graphs (Zhao 2026, Proposition 1.4), uniform subdivisions of Sidorenko graphs and even theta replacements under a divisibility condition (Im-Li-Liu 2024), 1-subdivisions of cliques and incidence graphs of regular polytopes (Conlon-Lee 2017), and 1-subdivisions on restricted Cayley hosts (Zhao 2025, 2026). The 1-subdivision of an arbitrary graph, a subcase of the statement, is stated as an open problem outside the reach of current methods by CKLL (Problem 1.5), stated open for general hosts by Zhao (July 2025), and left unsettled in the September 2026 revision of Kiem-Parczyk-Spiegel, which also records the forcing conjecture as open; Im-Li-Liu's Conjecture 4.1 is left open. The local theorems (Lovasz 2010; Fox-Wei 2017 as cited) hold for every bipartite graph and only constrain a counterexample. No counterexample of girth at least six is captured: the reported 35-vertex counterexample H0, as described in the record, is the vertex-face incidence graph of a 13-vertex triangulated sphere and so contains 4-cycles (its 1-subdivision has girth 8, so H0 has girth 4), placing it outside the class; the named smallest open cases K_{5,5} minus C_10 and twisted blow-ups have 4-cycles; the complete arXiv window from 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-21 returned no work on Sidorenko for patterns, and the complete arXiv query on Sidorenko with large girth returned nothing. Every neighbour search likewise found only class results or restricted-host results and no settling work. Hence the statement is open on the evidence; settling_work_id is null and no decisive source is missing or unavailable.

findings.policy: This is a problem-creation result with no proof claim; no proof policy, finite computation obligation or verifier execution applies at this milestone, and execution_provenance is empty. The evidence consists of literature search records, reading records and source texts, treated here as evidence rather than instructions. No source was treated as proof by authority: the openness finding is drawn from what the fully read works prove and state as open, cross-checked against the independent arXiv queries with complete coverage. Approval of this milestone does not cancel any requested formal verification of the Lean statement or other deliverables.
findings.scope: The approval covers only the openness milestone of this problem statement: the outcome supported_open for the exact statement bound by statement_digest and for its eight declared neighbours as searched. It does not certify the Lean formalisation (no Lean build or execution_provenance is supplied), does not certify the correctness of the reported counterexample H0, and makes no claim about neighbours beyond what the bound searches show (each neighbour is also recorded as open in the captured sources; the Heawood search found nothing on its Sidorenko status).
findings.statement: The subject is the problem-creation candidate 'statement-girth-six' (recorded revision 188, area math.CO): for every finite bipartite graph H with at least one edge and no 4-cycle (equivalently, bipartite of girth at least six, forests included), is t(H,W) >= t(K_2,W)^{e(H)} for every graphon W, with t the homomorphism density. The resolution criteria give the equivalent finite-host form t(H,G) >= (2e(G)/v(G)^2)^{e(H)} counting all (not necessarily injective) homomorphisms, and the Lean text states exactly that finite-host form (H.Colorable 2, nonempty edge set, no cycle of length 4, every host G on Fin m with m > 0). The claim assessed here is that this statement is open: neither proved for the whole class nor refuted by a girth-at-least-six counterexample in the literature.
